including media, culture, crime, the mafia—every aspect of society is controlled by this nexus of power. Also, corporations are at the outer edge. The people generate wealth because they work hard, creating more wealth in society. 

Think of society as a corporation: People are workers; elite families are owners; middle class manage operations. This metaphor isn't accurate but useful for analysis. Families own the nation, managers run it, and workers do the real labor.

When society rises, families let managers control society—democracy is when managers ensure better treatment of workers, leading to higher productivity and happiness. However, with elite overproduction, too many children want powerful positions, putting the corporation in debt. Managers exploit people instead of advocating for them.

Managers engage in rent-seeking behavior, like a lawyer collecting rent from clients or a middle-class professional profiting from their specialized role. During decline, managers push workers harder to maintain their lifestyle and prove their worth, exploiting labor more.

Over time, elite factions form, competing for power, leading society into factional conflicts.
